# BlockQuery

> On-chain entity attribution for crypto trading desks, powered by Chainlabs. BlockQuery names the entity behind an on-chain transaction: the exchange, OTC desk, fund, miner, treasury or issuer behind an address, on both sides of a transfer.

BlockQuery sells two things:

- OTC VIP monitoring. Ongoing monitoring of an OTC desk's counterparty book, delivered as weekly or monthly written reports for a fixed monthly fee. It shows where a desk's counterparties trade when they are not trading with the desk: the room to grow existing accounts, named prospects moving size through competing venues, and accounts that have started routing elsewhere. Nothing to integrate. https://www.blockquery.io/
- Entity data feeds. The attribution layer delivered as data you own: multi-year history as CSV or parquet, a live API in the identical schema, an optional mempool feed, and point-in-time attribution so a backtest only sees what was knowable at the time. Bitcoin first, additional chains on request. https://www.blockquery.io/data

## Key facts

- 18,000 commercial entities attributed
- 800+ OTC desks and 480+ regional exchanges attributed
- 30+ blockchains covered
- 90,000 addresses attributed through direct research; hundreds of millions more through entity clustering (312M+ on Bitcoin, 47M+ on Ethereum, 94.4M+ on Tron)
- Around 300 new attributions added monthly
- Every attribution is human-verified by a team of intelligence analysts and carries verifiable source evidence
- Chainlabs has been building entity attribution continuously for six years
- Clients include Coinbase and OKX
- BlockQuery does not predict price and does not sell trading signals. It sells data and monitoring.
